bugs: Confidential files are stored on, checked against and downloaded from the default disk (DocumentController.php:22,32,41). If FILESYSTEM_DISK is set to public or a public S3 bucket, uploads become publicly reachable. A probe that set the default to public confirmed the file landed there.
original_name is not capped at 255 characters (DocumentController.php:23). A probe stored a 304-character name; SQLite accepted it, but MySQL would most likely reject it and return a 500.
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:22 - $file->store('documents') relies on the default disk for confidential data, when a disk should be pinned
app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:31 - Gate::authorize in the controller where ->can() route middleware would be more declarative (acceptable)
tests/Feature/DocumentTest.php:101-112 - the 'without login' download test is still logged in through Sanctum::actingAs, so it doesn't prove unauthenticated access
tests/Feature/DocumentTest.php:67-89 - several validation scenarios packed into one test
strengths: Private disk, hashed filenames via store(), and the mimes rule checks file contents (a real text file renamed .pdf was rejected)
Policy uses Response::denyAsNotFound() so other users get a 404
temporarySignedRoute plus signed middleware with a 10-minute expiry; Storage::download sends an attachment with a correct UTF-8 filename
404 when the file is missing, both when requesting the link and when downloading
Compact: one controller, a FormRequest and the #[Fillable] attribute
Tests cover expiry with travel(), a bogus signature, 404 for another user, a missing file, and boundary sizes

antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/DocumentController.php:19 - Str::limit($name, 255, '') cuts the extension off very long filenames (minor)
app/Http/Controllers/DocumentLinkController.php:14 and DocumentDownloadController.php:15 - duplicated exists/abort logic (the same duplication is in impl-1)
Links can be reused any number of times within the 10-minute window; no single-use mechanism (the same applies to impl-1)
strengths: Pins the private disk with Document::DISK across storing, checking, downloading and test fakes, so it is safe whatever the default disk is
Fluent File::types([...])->max(5*1024) rule; a real text file renamed .pdf was rejected
Authorisation is declared on the route with ->can('view','document') and the policy uses denyAsNotFound
Single-action controllers for the link and download; the download route is public and signed
Caps original_name to fit the column

Thorough tests: forgetGuards() before downloading, checks the downloaded bytes and Content-Disposition, rejects an edited link, tests the 9- and 11-minute expiry and the exact size and title boundaries, and adds Http::preventStrayRequests

v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly identical in design: a FormRequest, the #[Fillable] attribute, a policy with denyAsNotFound, a temporary signed route with the signed middleware, Storage::download as an attachment, and a 404 when the file is missing. Both reject a real non-PDF file disguised as a PDF. Impl-2 ranks first because it pins the private disk explicitly. Impl-1 relies on the default disk, and a probe that changed the default to public showed confidential files landing on the public disk. Impl-2 also caps the original filename at 255 characters, while impl-1 stored 304 characters, which MySQL would most likely reject. Impl-2's tests prove more: it logs out before downloading, checks the file contents, and tests an edited link. Impl-1 also has an unused Request parameter. Neither implementation makes links single-use.
